meta.description: BNY analysis: record $5.7B quarterly revenue, guidance raised on both fee income and NII, dividend up 19%: against a CFO who just sold his entire direct stake. A-, buy the EMA20 retest, not the high.
meta.ogDescription: BNY raised its full-year guide on every line that matters and hiked the dividend 19%. The level where the trade works, and the insider print you should know about.

header.name: The Bank of New York Mellon

verdict.summary: BNY is the quiet compounder of the custody world: a record $5.7B revenue quarter in July, fees up 10.8%, net interest income up 20.2%, and a guidance raise on every line that matters; full-year revenue to +10-11%, NII to +12-13%, roughly 400 basis points of positive operating leverage. The board underlined it with a 19% dividend hike. The chart matches the story: a three-week base above a rising EMA stack, with the late-July flush to 151.68 bought back in two sessions. Two honest counterweights. The upside to the 52-week high at 163.77 is modest from here, so an at-market buyer is paid poorly against a proper stop. And the insider tape carries a real footnote: the CFO sold 31,800 shares on July 29 (about $4.9M, roughly a tenth of his direct stake) two weeks after the raise; four other officers sold ~$6.6M in April. The CEO's July filing at 161.07, easy to misread as a top-tick sale, was a transfer into a family trust with no change in ownership. Neither breaks the thesis; both say the easy part of the move is behind. The trade is the retest of the EMA20 zone near 155.50, stop under the July flush, first target the annual high.

business.overview: BNY is the world's largest custodian, safekeeping and servicing roughly $50 trillion of assets, clearing US Treasuries, and running Pershing (wealth infrastructure) and a $2T asset manager. The model is fee-heavy with an NII kicker: scale platforms that grow with market levels and activity, plus a balance sheet that reprices with rates. The July quarter showed both engines running, record revenue, fees and NII both double-digit — and management raised the full-year outlook on revenue, NII and operating leverage simultaneously.
business.moat: Custody is an oligopoly with brutal switching costs; Treasury clearing is near-infrastructure. The moat is not the question: the multiple already knows.
business.theme: Fee compounders with rate optionality; capital returned, not hoarded.

earnings.beatNote: Five consecutive beats (Q2 2025 verified separately: 1.94 vs 1.74). The July 15 report gapped the stock +5.1% on twice normal volume, the market believed the raise. Next report: October 15, outside the trade window.

insiders.signal: Zero buys against eight sales in 120 days, with the two most senior officers selling into the two strongest tapes of the year. The CFO keeps ~$39M of unvested exposure, so this reads as profit-taking rather than abandonment; but informed sellers at 154-161 define the zone where fresh money should not chase.

technicals.setupNote: The July 15 guidance gap (+5.1% on 2x volume) built a three-week base between 152.50 and 160.86 under the annual high at 163.77. The July 29 flush to 151.68; the CFO-sale session, was bought back within two sessions, which is what strong bases do. Price now trades in the upper third of the range, 2.2% above the EMA20, with MACD below its signal: consolidation, not acceleration. The clean entry is the EMA20 retest near 155; the alternative is a confirmed close above 160.86 that puts the annual high in play immediately.

macro.regime: Risk-on (VIX 15.9). ISM services Aug 5, US jobs report Aug 7.
macro.impact: BNY's NII guide assumes market-implied rates as of June 30 — a violent rate repricing in either direction dents one engine or the other (NII vs fee-sensitive market levels). At beta 1.06 the name is calmer than the banks; a hot jobs print is a wobble, not a thesis-breaker.

risks.riskSummary: Balance-sheet risk is minimal: no dilution, low short interest, capital returning. The live risks are positioning ones: senior insiders selling into strength, momentum cooling inside the base, and a premium multiple that assumes the guide is met.

riskCards.title: C-Suite Selling Into Strength
points: CFO sold 100% of direct holdings July 29 (~$4.9M); retains ~$39M unvested
CEO sold ~$4.0M at 161.07, the top-tick session after the raise
April cluster (GC + SEVP, ~$5.8M) the day after the Q1 print; zero buys in 120 days
riskCards.verdict: Profit-taking with a message: the people running the company sold at 154-161. Buy below their prints, not above them.

The guidance catalyst is consumed; next dated event is October 15
riskCards.verdict: Bases resolve both ways. The EMA20 entry with a stop under 151.68 keeps the failure cheap.

riskCards.title: Premium Multiple, Priced Execution
points: P/B 2.69x and 15.3x forward is the top of the custody group
The NII guide leans on June 30 rate assumptions and last-cycle deposit betas
Any fee-market wobble (equity levels, activity) trims the revenue guide's cushion
riskCards.verdict: Nothing here is cheap-with-a-catalyst; this is quality-at-a-fair-price. Size accordingly.

tradeIdea.statusNote: Intraday 158.40 leaves ~3.4% to the annual high against a ~4.5% stop; the at-market math fails. Limit order at the EMA20 retest.
tradeIdea.entryNote: The 155-156 zone stacks the EMA20 (154.96) with the base's midline. Enter on a hold of that zone. Alternative: a confirmed daily close above 160.86 (base top) puts 163.77 in play immediately, half size there, stop under 156.
tradeIdea.thesis: Every line of the July report argues for higher — record revenue, double raise, 19% dividend hike. The tape argues for patience: insiders sold 154-161 and momentum is resting. The retest entry reconciles both: own the raise at the average, with the stop under the flush the base already absorbed.
